title: Three-point basis vectors
statement: Let $\phi_0,\phi_1,\phi_2$ be the three-point Fourier functions on the equally weighted set $\{a,b,c\}$, given by $\phi_0=1$, $\phi_1(a)=\sqrt2$ and $\phi_1(b)=\phi_1(c)=-\sqrt2/2$, and $\phi_2(a)=0$, $\phi_2(b)=\sqrt6/2$, $\phi_2(c)=-\sqrt6/2$. The $j$th vector of the three-point Fourier basis is the function $\phi_j$, for every $j\in\{0,1,2\}$.
